 'We definitely deserved to score' published at 19:17 GMT 19:17 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal 
 Liverpool 
 Andoni Iraola, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live: "Disappointing for us. We definitely deserved to score but weren't able. We regret the first 15 minutes until we conceded the goal but I loved after. We changed a little bit by being more brave and aggressive and we put them under pressure. We had some chances that we haven't finished properly. Also they have been good defensively."
 On refereeing decisions: "I think the Alexander Isak penalty was very clear. Everyone sees how they grab the shirt. I don't understand. I think it's because he doesn't dive. The shame is that we have to tell our players to dive. It is so clear and it is a great chance for us."
 On a potential red card for Arsenal. "I've just seen one replay. I think a red card has to be more clear movement. It didn't look like a clear red card, no.
 "There are a lot of positives but it's not enough against these teams. We had very good situations inside the box that we haven't finished properly but I value how we played after the 1-0 a lot."
 On the momentum going in the right direction: "It's difficult to say after a loss, coming from five wins. This game was important for us and it feels disappointing."

 'This is why we do what we do' published at 19:14 GMT 19:14 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, speaking to Sky Sports: "Extremely proud. It's been 14 years, that's a long time. I'm sure we made everybody attached to the club extremely proud today. Not only for the victory but for the way we've done it, the spirit we've shown. Especially considering what happened four days ago when you lose and go out of the cup against a team you are supposed to beat. That's the magical part of this game, it can take you to really bad places but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic and we've done it.
 "The game is going to turn in a different direction very quickly. The way they attack, they can generate vertical attacks almost from a bad clearance or a bad throw, that's the quality that they have. And you have to be prepared, immediately to react to that with 60 metres to defend with four or five players running into your box. And we discussed that, we put everything into those actions, sometimes with more quality, sometimes with less quality, and we generated our own chaos. 
 "But, as well I think we have to give credit to the players for the situations and chances today that we didn't put away. Overall, to win against a team that is producing what they are doing, and also in the emotional state after Fleetwood, that's what a winning team should do."
 On Anfield's atmosphere: "You have to go through that, otherwise you don't win. We have had previous like that in the past and hadn't sustained it. We made a penalty or misread in the box or sometimes they have a magical moment and put the ball in the net and you don't manage to win the game. Today we had all of that, we had an element of luck as well and we had the quality in the right moments as well to hurt them."
 On Liverpool not getting a penalty for a shirt pull on Alexander Isak: "No, I haven't seen that."
 On what this win means for the title race: "Today is too early. Let's enjoy this incredible victory with the players and staff and tomorrow we start to prepare for another big, big night in Prague.
 On what the win means as a manager: "I'm extremely proud; this is something you want to accomplish. That's the challenge and mission you want to accomplish. I love it when it's something we have not done for many years. It was the same with Chelsea away and Manchester United away. To be able to beat all those, that's the purpose and motivation and why we do what we do."

 'What the team has done here today is incredible' published at 19:11 GMT 19:11 GMT 
 Liverpool v Arsenal (16:30 GMT) 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "This was especially for everyone attached to this football club. Fourteen years without winning here is a long time. We just said after the last few days, after the defeat against Fleetwood, that things happen for a reason and that's going to give us another spring and hunger and belief to go and do it. What the team has done here today is incredible.
 "It was very fluid at times, we generated six or seven chances. But the game becomes very chaotic once we misplace passes, a clearance, these guys are running at you. It's incredible the ability they have to generate vertical attacks. But the way the team sustained that kind of game is incredible for me.
 "They are in a really good moment. It was really deserved, to come here and win in the manner that we have done, I think the players deserve so much credit."
 On Declan Rice's assist : "Not just that, first of all, the movement to recognise the open situation to make the overlap, the timing of him playing the two vs one in the right manner and arriving from the far side constantly in the right space is something we discussed. In the second half, we had two big chances, there were a lot of moments where the team had some incredible actions."

 'We can all see that he holds the shirt' published at 19:07 GMT 19:07 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, speaking to Sky Sports o n the penalty appeals: "Especially the Alex [Isak] one. Gakpo was sustained holding, I understand. The Alex one is a clear penalty. You hold the shirt, we can all see that he holds the shirt. Because he doesn't go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty. I don't understand it.
 On if Isak should have gone down: "That's the problem we have with the game. Because he doesn't dive and go to the floor. The fact that you are even asking me if he should go to the floor, if he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100%. It should be like this but it is what it is. Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it."
 On if he will tell Isak to do that: "Yes, definitely."

 'If you don't dive they won't call it' published at 19:06 GMT 19:06 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, speaking to BBC Sport: "We wanted another result definitely today. We are to the blame, especially from the beginning of the game. After we conceded the goal probably you had nothing to protect so you play more freely, we played more brave and I think we turned the game in the first half, we finished very well. We tried it in the second half but were unable to score.
 "We had good chances - we hit the crossbar and had good situations we were not able to finish. We definitely deserved a goal.
 "I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down. We finished the first half very well, kept pushing. I loved a lot of moments of the game.
 "We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today. A lot of games to play."
 On not getting any penalty shouts, especially when Alexander Isak had his shirt pulled inside the box: "It got seen. There is a clear grab the shirt. Alex was just in front of him, he was going to head in front of the goal but couldn't because he had the shirt. I don't understand why they didn't call it, probably because he has not gone to the floor.
 "I think the Gakpo one was not a penalty but the Alex one he was going to head the ball in front of the goalkeeper. He grabbed the shirt. I don't understand why it wasn't called.
 "You have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it."

 'It was a clear penalty' published at 19:00 GMT 19:00 GMT 
 Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk, speaking to Sky Sports: "Disappointment. We play at home, we had some opportunities. We tried everything. We could have done a bit better in the last 15 minutes to get more balls in the box. It wasn't enough today and that's why disappointment is the feeling I'm having.
 "When we conceded we played much better. Alexis could have changed the game."
 On if Alexander Isak should have been awarded a penalty: "I think it was a clear penalty. I've seen it back and I've seen it being given. Today it wasn't meant to be.
 On if Isak should have reacted more: "We have 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras. Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal."
 On the team's momentum: "When someone new comes in the building and everything changes, it just needs time. I'm pretty sure things will click and things will work out.

 Figure caption, Arsenal move clear at the top with a rare win at Liverpool
 By Gary Rose BBC Sport journalist Arsenal took advantage of Manchester City's defeat by Brighton as they edged a thrilling encounter at Liverpool to move three points clear at the top of the Premier League. 
 Back-to-back losses for City handed the Gunners the opportunity to seize control of the title race, but they faced a difficult task against a rapidly improving Reds.
 They broke the deadlock in the 16th minute when Declan Rice's ball across the face of goal was turned in by Kai Havertz at the back post.
 But after that Arsenal had to withstand wave after wave of Liverpool attacks for the rest of the first half as the home side looked to get back level.
 David Raya just got to Virgil van Dijk's flick-on when Alexander Isak was set to pounce and the Reds had two penalty claims waved away before Florian Wirtz crashed a free-kick against the crossbar.
 Liverpool maintained their dominance early in the second half but Arsenal's defence had tightened up considerably and left very few opportunities for the Reds to exploit. 
 The introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly saw Arsenal regain the momentum in the latter stages and only a brilliant one-handed save by Alisson prevented Christos Tzolis making it 2-0 with a fine first-time strike towards the far corner.
 Ultimately, Havertz's early goal was enough for Arsenal to take all three points as they celebrated a first win at Liverpool in the Premier League since 2012.
 The loss for Liverpool means they are fifth but nine points behind leaders Arsenal.
 I'll tell my players to dive in future - Iraola 
 Published 1 hour ago 
 Brilliant defensive display seals Arsenal win 
 Figure caption, Mikel Arteta post-match interview - Liverpool v Arsenal
 This game could best be described as having been defence versus attack, with Arsenal spending pretty much the entire match repelling Liverpool advances.
 Scoring goals is pivotal to getting wins but so too is a strong defence, and the Gunners showed they have that in this game.
 They rode their luck at times in the first half but they were nevertheless impressive at the back, keeping their discipline and shape when it may have been easy to wilt against Liverpool's strong press.
 After the shock loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup in midweek, Arsenal needed a performance that highlighted such a display as a mere blip, and this was certainly that.
 Liverpool had 17 attempts on goal but could not manage any on target and Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players gleefully celebrated a huge win at the final whistle.
 Liverpool impress but lack clinical touch 
 Figure caption, Andoni Iraola post-match interview - Liverpool v Arsenal
 This was a defeat for Liverpool that leaves them some way off the pace in the title race, but there were still plenty of reasons for their fans to leave Anfield feeling optimistic.
 The team and style of football Andoni Iraola is looking to create has become more and more obvious in the past few games and it is an exciting prospect.
 Their pace on the attack and high press left Arsenal under near constant pressure in the first half, during which they had appeals for penalties waved away when Jurrien Timber pulled Isak's shirt inside the box, while Cody Gakpo went down after a tussle with Christos Tzolis.
 But for all their good work in building up attacks they were just not clinical enough, with Isak - who has six goals in the Premier League this season - particularly quiet.
 But they will not face a defence like Arsenal's often, and this defeat was only their second this season.
 From Fleetwood embarrassment to 'magical' Anfield win 14 years in making
